subject: Sandboxization & VPC mesh: tenant separation and persistent-tiering playbook
messages:
From: Platform Ops <platform-ops@stratusworks.io>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: devops_lead@stratusworks.io
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sandboxization reqs: cluster topology, VPC mesh and storage tiers

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the kickoff call earlier. Per our internal alignment I wanted to capture StratusWorks' constraints and ask for a recommended "sandboxization" playbook for our on-prem clusters. Key bullets:

- We need tenant-level sandboxes for product teams (dev, staging, qa) inside our VPC-only private deployment; network must prevent east-west access between tenant sandboxes except through controlled egress/proxy.
- Persistent data policy: short-lived PVCs for dev (7d TTL), long-lived for staging (90d), archive to NFS/object store for retention beyond 90d.
- Some workloads require local SSD for KV caches (low-latency), others need high-throughput blockstore for model artifacts.
- Encryption at rest with our AWS KMS (customer-managed key) across CIFS/NFS and blockstore; we also require pod-level secrets to never leave cluster.
- DNS must be split-horizon; internal services only resolvable within tenant VPC segments.
- Service mesh? Product engineering prefers mTLS for staging but wants a lighter-weight approach for dev.

Can Redwood provide a concrete node-pool layout, storage-class definitions (CSI choices), CNI recommendation (security posture + egress controls), and a short rollout checklist for preflight validation? Also please flag any limitations we should be aware of for snapshots/sizing during backups.

Appreciate a short draft by EOD tomorrow so we can route to procurement/security.

Thanks,
Maya (Platform Ops)
StratusWorks

--
platform-ops@stratusworks.io

From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Platform Ops <platform-ops@stratusworks.io>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sandboxization reqs: cluster topology, VPC mesh and storage tiers

Maya,

Thanks — good summary. Attaching a concise playbook and an initial network drawing (PDF) and PV/QoS matrix (XLSX). High-level recommendations below; I'll follow up with a preflight checklist and rollback guidance.

1) Topology & node-pools (recommended):
   - control-plane: 3x dedicated masters, no user workloads, isolated management network
   - infra-pool: 3–5 medium VMs (monitoring, logging, ingress controllers, CSI controllers)
   - tenant-slices (per-tenant logical node-pools):
     * dev-slice: small instances, preemptible allowed, tainted (dev=true:NoSchedule), ephemeral SSD for local cache (emptyDir+localPV fallback), evictionPriority=low
     * staging-slice: medium instances, reserved capacity, standard block PV, retention=90d, QoS: Guaranteed/High
     * prod-slice (if you map staging->prod later): large instances, dedicated NICs, encrypted blockstore, QoS: Highest

   Notes: use node selectors and RBAC to restrict kubelet-level label changes. For true tenant isolation we map RBAC/NetworkPolicies to node-pool labels and enforce admission via PodSecurityPolicy replacement (OPA Gatekeeper) and RuntimeClass restrictions.

2) CNI & VPC mesh:
   - Recommendation: Cilium in L3 mode with ClusterMesh for cross-site visibility and eBPF policy enforcement.
   - Enforce strict egress via an egress gateway (NAT + proxy) per tenant slice; block direct cross-tenant pod-to-pod traffic except through explicitly whitelisted services and the egress proxy ports.
   - For split-horizon DNS, deploy CoreDNS instances per tenant slice and use DNS-over-TLS between nodes and the authoritative internal resolver.

3) Storage classes & CSI drivers:
   - local-ssd: CSI-local for KV caches (ReadWriteOnce, volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer), use ephemeral TTL controller to cleanup stale localPV
   - block-encrypted: CSI for your blockstore (iSCSI/Fibre) with KMS key integration — enable volume-level encryption and snapshot support; storageClass reclaimPolicy=Delete for dev, Retain for staging/archive migration
   - nfs-archive: use NFS v4 with an object-tier gateway for long-term archive; retention lifecycle policy triggered by snapshot->copy job to object store.

4) Snapshotting & backups:
   - Use Velero with plugin for your blockstore; schedule frequent snapshots for staging during business hours (every 2h) and hourly DB dumps for prod.
   - Note: local-ssd volumes cannot be snapshotted; design jobs to flush caches to blockstore before snapshot windows.

5) Service mesh strategy:
   - Staging: Istio with mTLS enabled and strict mutual TLS policy to validate behavior under secure comms.
   - Dev: recommend a lightweight sidecarless approach (Cilium L7 policies) to avoid mesh overhead; you can enable a small per-tenant Istio in a later canary.

6) Operational guardrails & security:
   - Admission: OPA Gatekeeper + mutating webhook to inject user-allowed annotations and enforce resource quotas.
   - KMS: integrate your AWS KMS via Redwood agent running in control plane VPC; key usage logs forwarded to your SIEM.
   - Audit logs: configure kube-audit to ship to central logging with sensitive scrubbers for secrets.

If this aligns I'll prepare the preflight checklist (hardware, NIC bonding, MTU checks, NTP, CRI config, kubelet flags, CSI driver pre-installs) and a short deployment runbook for a canary tenant.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Sandboxization reqs: cluster topology, VPC mesh and storage tiers

Maya / team,

Quick additions from an operational standpoint:

- Node-sizing guidance: prefer localNVMe *for* dev KV caches (at least one 1TB NVMe per dev-node); staging block volumes should target 3–5 IOPS/GB depending on model artifact read patterns.
- Eviction/oom thresholds: set kube-reserved and system-reserved aggressively on staging nodes to avoid eviction cascades during heavy model pulls.
- PVC binding: use WaitForFirstConsumer for staged deployments to ensure topology-aware provisioning.
- Monitoring endpoints: per-tenant Prometheus remote_write to your central cluster with tenant labels; keep scrape intervals longer for dev to reduce cardinality.
- Network perf testing: before cutover run a 72h soak with simulated multi-tenant traffic (we can provide a test harness).

Attachment: PV QoS matrix contains suggested IO profiles for modeling costs.

I'll draft the preflight checklist later tonight and include the exact CRI/CRI-O vs containerd tuning flags we've validated.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Engineering Manager, On-Prem Deployments, Redwood Inference
